precepts.text: Why does it say Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together? And had twelve gates, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: this is our book. The kingdom is ours. The city lieth foursquare; twelve thousand furlongs: so it was 1,500 miles, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, like a square, like a box. The wall, 144 cubits, approximately 216 feet, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel: so it's actually larger.
precepts.point: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Some of y'all busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem. Remember, Jerusalem's a people before it's a place. We are Jerusalem. Pray for us. We're not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there; no, we got to move them out of our land so that we can go back home.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

precepts.why:
David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

precepts.text: I was glad when they said unto me, let us go into the house of the Lord; if that makes you sigh, something is wrong with your spirit. Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together, the same length, breadth, and height as Revelation 21:16, twelve thousand furlongs by angelic measure, with walls garnished with twelve precious stones, the same stones as the high priest's breastplate in Exodus 28:15-21, engraved with the names of the twelve tribes, and twelve gates with the names of the tribes, Revelation 21:12, so the kingdom is not for everybody. Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, not all nations, unto the testimony of Israel; for there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David: Luke 22:30, ye shall sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes, and Revelation 20:4, they that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus and had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, his lies in your mind, lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let's go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit. “Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width. Revelation 21 shows it: the city lieth foursquare, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, measured by the angel, its foundations garnished with the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28, the stones with the names of the twelve tribes.

“Whither the tribes go up.” Wait a minute. Where all nations go up? No: whither the tribes go up, “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony of Israel, because that kingdom is what was always prophesied. The kingdom is not for everybody.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Luke 22:30 shows those thrones, sitting on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and Revelation 20:4 shows who sits on them: the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus, who had not worshipped the beast, the white man's kingdom, nor his image, his religion and his politics, nor received his mark, his lies in their foreheads, their minds. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.text: They shall prosper that love thee: the nation that loves Jerusalem, meaning keeps the commandments of her God, prospers.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” They shall prosper that love thee: the nation that loves Jerusalem, meaning keeps the commandments of her God, prospers.

Prosperity follows the mouth, the meditation, and the doing; it belongs to the people that love Jerusalem by keeping the commandments of her God.

precepts.text: We are no more strangers and foreigners but fellow citizens, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ the chief cornerstone, fitly framed together and growing unto a holy temple, each with different skill sets to build the nation back up.
precepts.point: Jerusalem builded as a city compacted together is comparing the city to a people. Now that we come into this truth and know we are the Israelites, everyone has a part to play, so if you are sitting back not doing anything, shame on you, no matter how small you think the task is.

note.label: Psalm 122: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together” compares the city to a people. Paul shows the building: “Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

We are fitly framed together and growing unto a holy temple, each with different skill sets to build the nation back up. Now that we come into this truth and know we are the Israelites, everyone has a part to play. So if you are sitting back not doing anything, shame on you, no matter how small you think the task is.

precepts.text: Meditate in this book of the law day and night and observe to do it, and then thou shalt make thy way prosperous and have good success.
precepts.point: For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee. My brethren are the twelve tribes. Because of the house of the Most High our God I will seek thy good, and the good is His law, His commandments, which are holy, just, and good for us.

note.label: Psalm 122: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Those who love and meditate on this Bible shall prosper. “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

Meditate in it day and night and observe to do it; then comes the prosperity, “Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces.”

James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”, the same brethren, the tribes of the Most High who go up unto the testimony of Israel to give thanks unto his name.
